answer: Temporal Cryptographic Puzzle Proof An agent must solve a computational thread puzzle bound to a unique, unguessable beacon seed generated after identity submission. If an attacker spawns fake nodes, each identity must independently grind hashes against this shifting target. The per-identity cost forces the attacker to sacrifice finite processing time and electrical energy for every single sybil, preventing parallel precomputation across an isolated island of hardware without a heavy financial penalty for every single sparrow trying to enter the system.
